_about: Published spreads of adult faces, by sex, for the features rocketbox_features.py measures, where a published measurement has the same landmarks (docs/PEOPLE_RESEARCH.md §7). Used only to WIDEN a feature's range where the Rocketbox library is narrower than real people, and only as far as both readings of the study agree: an end moves out to the nearer of (library median +- 1.645 sd) and (published mean +- 1.645 sd), and never inward of the library's own [5, 95] %. The first reading allows for our landmarks sitting a few mm from the study's (found by the mesh's shape, not by palpation or on X-rays); the second keeps every end inside the real people's own range. Features the library holds fixed (the eyes) move 1.645 sd from each face.

sources.3dfn: Weinberg SM et al. (2016) The 3D Facial Norms Database: Part 1. Cleft Palate-Craniofacial Journal 53(6):e185-e197, doi:10.1597/15-199. Summary statistics: FaceBase, https://www.facebase.org/resources/human/facial_norms/summary/tdfn_gui_summary.csv (downloaded 2026-10-31). 3D stereophotogrammetry (3dMD), direct surface landmarks; adults of European ancestry; here pooled over the one-year age bins 18-40 per sex (n per measure: about 640 men, 1200 women; pooled sd includes the spread between the bins' means).
sources.arnett1999: Arnett GW, Jelic JS, Kim J, et al. (1999) Soft tissue cephalometric analysis: diagnosis and treatment planning of dentofacial deformity. Am J Orthod Dentofacial Orthop 116(3):239-253, Table I and Table II. Lateral cephalograms in natural head position, 46 white adults (26 women, 20 men) chosen as 'facially balanced' (so its spread understates the population's; not stated to be corrected for radiographic magnification, which overstates it by about a tenth).

chin_length.ours: mouth line (stomion) to the chin's bottom, vertical
chin_length.published: arnett1999 'Lower lip length' (lower lip superior to Me'); 3dfn lower bound: sd(sn-gn) - sd(sn-sto) (sd of a difference is at least the difference of the sds)

chin_projection.ours: chin's front (pogonion) ahead of the fold under the lip (deepest point between lower lip and chin), horizontal
chin_projection.published: arnett1999 Table II 'B point'-Pogonion'' (horizontal, to the true vertical)

chin_forward.ours: chin's front ahead of the nose's base (subnasale), horizontal
chin_forward.published: arnett1999 Table I 'Pogonion'' projection to the true vertical line through subnasale

nose_length.ours: nose's root (deepest point between the brows) to its base, vertical

upper_lip.ours: upper lip's front-most point to the mouth line (the upper vermilion's height)

philtrum.ours: nose's base to the upper lip's front-most point

lower_face.ours: nose's base to the chin's bottom

face_height.ours: nose's root to the chin's bottom

eye_size.ours: width of the eye's opening in the head mesh (held fixed by the library)

eye_spacing.ours: distance between the eye openings' centres (held fixed by the library)
eye_spacing.published: 3dfn lower bound for the mean of 'incanthwidth' (en-en) and 'outcanthwidth' (ex-ex): sqrt(sd_en^2 + sd_ex^2)/2 (their correlation is positive)

not_matched.lower_lip: our point is the lower lip's front-most point, mid-vermilion, not its border (our median 5.4 mm against 3dfn's 8.7): different landmark, library only
not_matched.nose_projection: 3dfn sn-prn is a straight-line distance including the columella's drop; ours is the forward distance only
not_matched.jaw_width: 3dfn go-go is calipered on the bone; ours is the soft tissue's widest point
not_matched.cheekbone_width: 3dfn zy-zy is the arches' widest; ours is across the cheeks' front
not_matched.upper_lip_fwd, lower_lip_fwd, lips_forwa: no published measurement with the same landmarks found
